At this rate, on which day would the number of bacteria per milliliter reach \x3Cspan>\x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"5 point 1 2, times 10, to the power 8\">\x3C/span>\x3C/span>?\x3C/p>",rationale:"\x3Cp>Choice D is correct. The number of bacteria per milliliter is doubling each day. For example, from day 1 to day 2, the number of bacteria increased from 2.5 &times; 10\x3Csup>5\x3C/sup> to 5.0 &times; 10\x3Csup>5\x3C/sup>. At the end of day 3 there are 10\x3Csup>6\x3C/sup> bacteria per milliliter. At the end of day 4, there will be&nbsp;10\x3Csup>6\x3C/sup> &times; 2 bacteria per milliliter. At the end of day 5, there will be (10\x3Csup>6 \x3C/sup>&times; 2) &times; 2, or 10\x3Csup>6\x3C/sup> &times; (2\x3Csup>2\x3C/sup>) bacteria per milliliter, and so on. At the end of day \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span>, the number of bacteria will be 10\x3Csup>6 \x3C/sup>&times; (2\x3Csup>\x3Cspan>d\x3C/span> &ndash; 3\x3C/sup>). If the number of bacteria per milliliter will reach 5.12 &times; 10\x3Csup>8\x3C/sup> at the end of day \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span>, then the equation \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"10 to the power 6, end power, times 2 to the power d minus 3, end power, equals 5 point 1 2, times 10 to the power 8\">\x3C/span> must hold. Since 5.12 &times; 10\x3Csup>8\x3C/sup> can be rewritten as 512 &times; 10\x3Csup>6\x3C/sup>,&nbsp; the equation is equivalent to \x3Cspan>\x3Cimg align=\"middle\" role=\"math\" class=\"math-img\" src=\"data:image/png;base64,\" alt=\"2 to the power d minus 3, end power, equals 512\">\x3C/span>. Rewriting 512 as 2\x3Csup>9\x3C/sup> gives \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span> &ndash; 3 = 9, so \x3Cspan>d\x3C/span> = 12. The number of bacteria per milliliter would reach 5.12 &times; 10\x3Csup>8\x3C/sup>&nbsp;at the end of day 12. \x3C/p>\x3Cp>Choices A, B, and C are incorrect.
